# `removed-std-api`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a standard-library path, however it is aliased, that the installed Zig
standard library provably no longer declares, naming the replacement when one is
known.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Code written for an older Zig keeps naming `std.fs.cwd`,
`std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator`, `std.Thread.Mutex` or
`std.io.fixedBufferStream` long after the standard library dropped them. The
compiler only reports such a name once the code is analyzed, and then without
saying what replaced it; this rule reports every use and names the replacement.

## When it fires

Paths are resolved through the same declaration index as
`deprecated-declaration`: `@import("std")` resolves to the installed standard
library, and the path is followed through constant namespace and type aliases
such as `const fs = std.fs;`, so `fs.cwd()`, `std.fs.cwd()` and
`@import("std").fs.cwd()` are all reported, once each, at the first member that
does not resolve.

A member is reported only when its namespace is a standard-library container the
index can list completely and nothing at its top level names the member: no
declaration, public or private, no field or enum value, and no
`usingnamespace`. Members reached through a value or parameter, namespaces
produced by a function call, `@Type`, `if` or `switch`, quoted `@"..."`
identifiers, and files outside the installed standard library are skipped.

Known removals name their replacement (`std.Io.Dir.cwd()`, `std.Io.Mutex`,
`std.heap.SafeAllocator`, `std.Io.Timestamp`, `std.Io.Reader.fixed`, the
arguments and environment of `std.process.Init`, `std.Io.net`, and others); the
table is checked against the pinned standard library. Other missing members are
reported without advice. When `modernize-deprecated-stdlib` is enabled it reports
a known removal written as a literal `std.…` path, with its fixes, and this rule
stays quiet there. The finding replaces the bare `unresolved-member` error the
module pass would report at the same member. Like imported deprecations, the
check runs in the CLI's cross-file pass and in the editor, not on a single file
in isolation, and offers no automatic edit.
